hero.title: Every customer conversation, in one place
hero.subtitle: WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram, Telegram, email, SMS and web chat arrive in a single shared inbox — routed to the right person, measured against your response targets, and answered with help from AI when you want it.
hero.reassurance: Start with one channel. Everything else has a sensible default you can change later.

channels.title: Wherever your customers already are
channels.note: Connect a channel once. From then on, messages arriving there become conversations automatically, and your reply goes back the way the customer came in — you never choose which channel to answer on.

how.title: How it works
how.subtitle: Four steps, from a customer's message to a reply you can measure.

arrives.title: It arrives
arrives.body: A customer messages you on any connected channel. It becomes a conversation in the shared inbox within seconds.

routed.title: It is routed
routed.body: Rules you write send it to the right queue. A catch-all rule is created with your workspace, so nothing can ever arrive with nowhere to go.

answered.title: It is answered
answered.body: An agent picks it up and replies, with AI drafting, summarising or translating alongside them. Simple questions can be answered by AI on its own.

measured.title: It is measured
measured.body: Four response clocks run against your targets, pausing outside your working hours, so you know where you stand before a customer tells you.

features.title: What you get
features.subtitle: Built for teams that answer customers all day, and for the people who have to report on it.

inbox.title: One shared inbox
inbox.body: Every channel in one list. Pick a conversation up, reply, add notes only your team sees, attach files, and transfer it when somebody else should take over.

ai.title: AI that knows when to stop
ai.body: Drafts replies, summarises long threads, translates, and can answer straightforward questions unattended. When it is unsure it hands over to a person rather than guessing.

routing.title: Routing that cannot drop anything
routing.body: Send conversations to the right queue by channel, keyword, language or customer. The catch-all rule underneath means nothing is ever lost.

sla.title: Response targets
sla.body: Four clocks — first response, next response, resolution and idle — each pausing outside your business hours, with a warning before you miss one.

customers.title: Customer history
customers.body: Everyone who has contacted you, with their whole history across every channel in one timeline, plus tags, notes and your own internal rating.

knowledge.title: Knowledge the AI answers from
knowledge.body: Articles and FAQs your AI draws on, so answers reflect what your company has actually decided rather than what a model guessed.

reports.title: Reporting
reports.body: Ten reports covering volume, speed, queues, satisfaction and AI use — from a live view of right now to an executive summary of the quarter.

intelligence.title: Patterns you would not have spotted
intelligence.body: The platform groups similar conversations and reports trends and unusual spikes, so you can see what customers keep asking about.

security.title: Enterprise controls
security.body: Role-based permissions on every action, complete separation between companies, encrypted credentials, and a permanent audit trail.

audience.title: Who uses it
audience.subtitle: From a two-person shop to a regulated institution.

smb.title: Small businesses
smb.body: One person answering WhatsApp and email without losing track of either.

enterprise.title: Enterprises
enterprise.body: Large teams split across departments, queues and service levels.

government.title: Government
government.body: Public-facing services with audit requirements and Arabic-first users.

healthcare.title: Healthcare
healthcare.body: Patient enquiries handled with a permanent record of who did what.

financial.title: Financial institutions
financial.body: Strict access control, complete audit trails, and the option to run AI locally so conversations never leave your systems.

honesty.title: What it does not do yet
honesty.subtitle: Worth knowing before you sign up rather than after.

items.mobile: There is no mobile app. The interface works in a phone browser and adapts to small screens, but there is nothing to install.
items.knowledge: Knowledge articles and FAQs are loaded and maintained for you rather than through a screen you edit yourself.
items.workflows: Automation rules are configured for you rather than built through a drag-and-drop editor.

cta.title: Start with one channel
cta.body: Create a workspace, connect a channel, and see a real conversation arrive. Everything else has a sensible default you can change later.

ai.title: An assistant that hands over instead of guessing
ai.body: The AI drafts replies, summarises long threads, translates, and can answer straightforward questions on its own. What makes it safe to switch on is what it does when it is unsure.

points.one: Answers only from your knowledge base, so replies reflect what your company has decided — not what a model inferred.
points.two: Stops and asks for a person when confidence is below the threshold you set.
points.three: Runs on OpenAI, Claude, or locally with Ollama so conversations never leave your systems.

ai.pullQuote: When it is not sure, it stops. A confident wrong answer costs more than a slow right one.

sla.title: Know you are late before the customer tells you
sla.body: Four clocks run against every conversation — first response, next response, resolution, and idle — and each one pauses outside your working hours.

points.one: Warnings arrive early enough to act on, not once the target has already gone.
points.two: Business hours and holidays are respected, so an evening message does not burn your target overnight.
points.three: A conversation in trouble is taken off AI automatically and handed to a person.

sla.pullQuote: An SLA nobody meets is ignored within a fortnight. Set targets you can keep, then watch them.

intelligence.title: See what your customers keep asking
intelligence.body: The platform reads finished conversations and groups the similar ones, then reports trends and unusual spikes. It tells you what is happening; you decide what to do about it.

points.one: Clusters show the questions that come up again and again, ranked by how often.
points.two: Trends and anomalies surface changes you would not spot one conversation at a time.
points.three: It observes only — it never changes how a conversation is handled or what the AI says.

intelligence.pullQuote: It shows you the question customers keep asking. Writing the answer down is still yours to do.

security.title: Built for organisations that get audited
security.subtitle: The controls regulated customers ask about first.

isolation.title: Complete separation
isolation.body: No company can reach another's data. Enforced on every single request, not by convention.

permissions.title: Permissions on every action
permissions.body: Roles decide what each person may do, and the server checks it every time — hiding a button protects nothing.

audit.title: A permanent audit trail
audit.body: Every significant action is recorded with who did it and when, and is never deleted.

local.title: Your data can stay put
local.body: Run the AI locally with Ollama and conversation content never leaves your own systems.

faq.title: Questions people ask before signing up

setup.q: How long does it take to set up?
setup.a: Minutes for the parts that matter. Your workspace is created with a queue, a service and a routing rule already in place, so the only genuinely required step is connecting one channel.

channels.q: Can I connect my existing WhatsApp number?
channels.a: You need WhatsApp Business API access through Meta rather than a personal number, and Meta's approval is not instant — worth starting early. Telegram takes about a minute if you want to try the platform today.

ai.q: Will the AI reply to customers without us?
ai.a: Only if you switch that on, and only when it is confident enough by a threshold you choose. Otherwise it drafts and one of your team sends. Nothing is ever sent without a person, unless you decide otherwise.

data.a: Into your own workspace, which no other company can reach. If you use OpenAI or Claude, conversation content goes to that provider when the AI is used; choose Ollama and it stays on your systems entirely.

languages.a: Yes — the whole interface, including right-to-left layout. Each person chooses their own language, so an Arabic-speaking agent and an English-speaking manager use the same workspace.

migrate.q: Can we bring our existing customers across?
migrate.a: There is no bulk import screen today. Customer records are created automatically the first time somebody contacts you, and if you use ERPNext, customers sync from there.

size.q: Is this only for large teams?
size.a: No. A one-person workspace works properly — you can complete setup without inviting anybody. It also handles departments, queues and service levels when you grow into them.

support.q: What happens if something goes wrong?
support.a: Every screen has help, every error explains what to do next, and every request carries a reference that lets an operator find exactly what happened rather than guessing.
